import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Router component that splits claims into three output ports based on ordered rules.
    Rules are evaluated in order; a row goes to the FIRST matching port only.
    Unmatched rows go to the default port.
    """
    claims = inputs["claims"].copy()
    
    # Initialize output dataframes
    fast_track = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    high_value = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    manual_review = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    standard = pd.DataFrame(columns=claims.columns)
    
    # Track which rows have been matched
    matched = pd.Series([False] * len(claims), index=claims.index)
    
    # Rule 1: amount <= 500 and photos_attached == 1
    rule1_mask = (~matched) & (claims["amount"] <= 500) & (claims["photos_attached"] == 1)
    fast_track = pd.concat([fast_track, claims[rule1_mask]], ignore_index=False)
    matched = matched | rule1_mask
    
    # Rule 2: amount > 10000
    rule2_mask = (~matched) & (claims["amount"] > 10000)
    high_value = pd.concat([high_value, claims[rule2_mask]], ignore_index=False)
    matched = matched | rule2_mask
    
    # Rule 3: photos_attached == 0 or amount > 500
    rule3_mask = (~matched) & ((claims["photos_attached"] == 0) | (claims["amount"] > 500))
    manual_review = pd.concat([manual_review, claims[rule3_mask]], ignore_index=False)
    matched = matched | rule3_mask
    
    # Unmatched rows go to default port (standard)
    standard = claims[~matched]
    
    # Reset indices to ensure clean output
    fast_track = fast_track.reset_index(drop=True)
    high_value = high_value.reset_index(drop=True)
    manual_review = manual_review.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Select only the specified columns for each output
    output_columns = ["claim_id", "amount", "photos_attached"]
    
    return {
        "claims_fast_track": fast_track[output_columns] if len(fast_track) > 0 else pd.DataFrame(columns=output_columns),
        "claims_high_value": high_value[output_columns] if len(high_value) > 0 else pd.DataFrame(columns=output_columns),
        "claims_manual_review": manual_review[output_columns] if len(manual_review) > 0 else pd.DataFrame(columns=output_columns)
    }
